texts: The operator records the dispensed weight of each raw material and confirms it with an e-signature.
Out-of-specification values are highlighted in red and raise a deviation automatically.
The system should warn the operator when a value is close to the limit.
Critical steps are verified before the batch continues.
A critical step must be verified by a second person who did not record it.
Entries must be recorded within the allowed time window after observation.
Entries must be recorded no later than 30 minutes after the observation time.
The supervisor can edit a recorded value.
A recorded value can be corrected only with a reason of at least 10 characters; the original stays visible.
It must be shown on the batch summary page.
The batch record loads quickly on shop-floor tablets.
The batch record page loads in under 2 seconds (p95) on the reference tablet.
QA can release a batch only when all steps are complete, verified and no deviation is open.
The batch is released after review.
Operators may skip non-critical steps.
Released batch records cannot be changed by any user.
The system displays the appropriate warning when a scale is out of calibration.
Weighing results are transferred from the balance automatically; manual entry is refused for critical weights.
TBD how yield is calculated for partial batches.
The yield must be between the limits defined in the master record.
QA can close a deviation after entering an investigation summary and signing.
Deviations are closed once the investigation is complete.
The deviation owner can delete a deviation raised in error.
A deviation raised in error can be voided by QA with a reason and e-signature; it stays in the audit trail.
CAPA actions must be completed in a timely manner.
CAPA actions must be completed within 30 days of approval unless QA grants an extension.
The CAPA effectiveness check is performed after a period defined by QA.
The system should send reminders before a CAPA is due.
The system sends an email reminder 7 days and 1 day before a CAPA due date.
Root cause categories include equipment, material, method, people, etc.
Deviations are classified as minor, major or critical by QA.
Critical deviations are escalated to the site head as soon as possible.
Critical deviations are escalated to the site head by email within 24 hours of classification.
They are notified when the deviation is classified as critical.
The investigation report can be modified after approval.
Every change request needs an impact assessment and approval before implementation.
The change request is approved by QA and the system owner before implementation.
Minor changes may be implemented without QA approval.
The system administrator can override the approval workflow if needed.
Emergency changes are documented retrospectively within 2 working days with QA approval.
The change history must be easy to review.
The change history shows who changed what, when, and why, for every change.
Only the latest approved version of an SOP is visible to operators.
Superseded SOPs are archived and retained for the required period.
Superseded SOPs are retained for 10 years after withdrawal.
The author can remove a document from the library.
Documents are reviewed periodically.
Each SOP is reviewed by its owner every 2 years; overdue reviews are shown on the QA dashboard.
This should be printed with a watermark.
Printed copies carry a watermark with the print date, the printing user and "uncontrolled copy".
The search must return relevant documents.
Document numbering format is TODO.
Users cannot execute a batch step unless they are trained on the current SOP version.
Training records are signed by the trainee and the trainer.
Training must be completed before the deadline.
The training matrix must be flexible enough for all departments.
Training assignments are generated automatically when a new SOP version becomes effective.
A trainer can change a failed assessment result to passed.
The dashboard must look modern.
Training completion should be tracked.
Analysts enter results against the specification; results outside the limits are flagged.
Results are checked before they are reported.
A second analyst reviews every result before it is reported to QA.
Analysts can reject a sample result and re-test.
Invalidating a result requires a laboratory investigation reference and QA e-signature.
Instrument data must be imported correctly.
Stability samples are pulled at the defined time points.
The sample queue should be sorted sensibly.
Samples must be tested within the hold time.
The chromatography integration parameters can be changed by the analyst.
Accounts lock after 3 consecutive failed login attempts.
Sessions expire after a period of inactivity.
Sessions expire after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Passwords must be strong.
Passwords have at least 12 characters and expire every 90 days.
The admin can deactivate a user account.
User accounts are never deleted; a leaver is deactivated with a reason, and the change is audit-trailed.
Role changes are approved before they take effect.
Access rights are reviewed by the system owner every 6 months.
The system must be secure.
The audit trail records user, date and time, action, old value, new value and reason.
The audit trail cannot be edited or deleted by any user, including administrators.
Audit trail entries are kept as long as needed.
QA reviews the audit trail of each batch before release.
The audit trail report may be exported to PDF.
The audit trail export must include all relevant fields.
Electronic signatures show the printed name, date, time and meaning of the signature.
It must be linked to the record it signs.
The weekly quality report is generated every Monday at 06:00 and emailed to QA managers.
Reports must support large data volumes.
The system handles up to 200 concurrent users with p95 response under 3 seconds.
The ERP interface should be robust.
Failed ERP messages are retried 3 times and then shown to the system owner for manual resolution.
Data is backed up regularly.
A full backup runs daily at 01:00 and a restore is tested every quarter.
The report layout is to be confirmed with the customer.
The dashboard shows open deviations, overdue CAPAs and batches awaiting release.
Users can filter the deviation list by status, severity, date range and product.
The system must be intuitive for shop-floor users.
Operators complete a batch step in no more than 3 clicks after scanning the material label.
